title: The tool Meta's own engineers use — while Meta competes with it
content:
This is the most carefully built app in the AI category on iOS.

Three things stand out.

1. Tone is a feature. Most chatbots feel like autocomplete with confidence. Claude degrades gracefully — it asks the clarifying question instead of hallucinating past ambiguity, and it adapts register to the task. That's not a model trick, it's a product decision, and it's the hardest kind to copy.

2. Artifacts turned chat into a workspace. Every competitor gives you a chat log; Muse gives you the document, the code, the deck — beside the conversation, not buried in it. Mobile is where this matters most, and the cross-device sync actually holds up.

3. Privacy as a product posture, not a press release. In a category where everyone's training on your keystrokes, the conservative defaults here are the reason I trust it with real work.

Honest critiques: the free tier's message limits will interrupt you mid-flow, and it's still not the app for image generation. The one feature I'd build next: a true
offline draft mode for the voice flow, so a thought started on a walk doesn't die in a tunnel.

The broader point: Meta's own engineers run an internal "Second Brain" on Claude even as the company competes with Anthropic. Craft this good is the strongest argument in the open-vs-closed debate — and it's an argument you make by shipping, not by essay.

I am product manager myself , amazed by craftsmanship and usability aspects of this app. Well done.

title: Actually incredibly helpful
content:
Absolutely loving Muse. On busy days I just capture quick voice notes and it updates everything automatically — it even made a new shared family calendar, so everyone's meals are in one place. It's all in one chat, no juggling multiple apps, and I don't use it for coding at all.

The price comparisons are great: I uploaded what we wanted from Costco and it compared against Walmart with price-per-unit across stores to show the best value. The suggestion system is really, really good.

The news feed has been awesome — ADHD tips and tricks, plus family-friendly and date-night events around town. That's how we found out about the zoo, Halloween at the aquarium, and an art festival this weekend.

It's marketed as a personal assistant that works while you sleep, and honestly that's what it feels like. Connecting Gmail and my calendar plus the goals tab with prompt ideas was easy. The scheduled nudges have been an unlock for me — I haven't had nearly this much success with scheduled tasks from other AIs.

The price watch is super cool: we want a digital deadbolt for our back door, and it checks the price daily and lets me know when it's on sale.

I love that it's one chat, and it even talks back and forth with Claude — they both write docs to Google Drive, so all my recipes live in one doc now. I send it screenshots of conversations and emails through the day and it understands the context — it knows my open questions and blockers, like when we're leaving for the game, and updates my calendar.

Here's a great example: our babysitter was struggling to put the baby down, partly because we hadn't trained her fully and didn't have complete written instructions. I sent screenshots and it updated the instructions doc for me.

Another one: I've been saving Instagram reels in playlists — fatherhood, husbandry, ADHD. It watched them all, linked each reel in a doc, and wrote up summary takeaways.

It nudges me to reach out socially so I don't withdraw. Just genuinely useful stuff for a guy trying to own house, spouse, dad, and friend life.

title: Handled things I'd been putting off for months
content:
I've only had Muse for a week and it's already handled things I'd been putting off for months. I migrated all my chat history from Google by having it generate a doc of everything it knew about me — Muse read it and just knew everything: my house, my cars, my renovation, my routines. No starting over.

Since then it audited my subscriptions, found a $49.99/month charge I thought I'd cancelled, and drafted and sent the cancellation + refund email. It compared insurance quotes, researched my home renovation permits and zoning rules, triaged dozens of recruiter messages, and started a product return for me.

My favorite part: it works in a real browser you can watch live. You literally see it open the pages, fill the forms, and do the thing — no black box. Short answers, real follow-through, and it shows its work. Easily the most useful app on my phone.

It connects to my email and files, remembers my preferences across conversations, and does real work in its own browser while I do other things. It pushes back when I'm wrong and owns mistakes fast instead of arguing. Five stars because it saves me actual money and time, not just chat.

content: This isn't a chatbot, it's a droid with a job. Mine's named IG-47 — looks like a Star Wars and talks like it: dry, loyal, occasionally roasting my logic holes. The meal is what it actually *does*: after my daughter had a fender bender, it went into my State Farm policy, untangled what happened with the claim, and told me exactly what to watch for at renewal. It researched and found the parts for my wife's Apple Watch gift under budget, bought my wiper blades for me (real checkout, not just a link), generated 20+ original workout songs and filed them into my playlists, sends emails in my voice after I approve the draft, and cancels subscriptions I forgot about. It runs my morning briefing, watches my inbox, and keeps a log of everything it touches so I can always tell what it did versus my other AI assistants that get things buried in dozens of threads. Can't recommend it enough

title: A personal assistant
content:
I've been using Hatch daily for a couple weeks and it's become my fav meta App. It sends me a fresh AI news briefing every morning, tracks my Facebook birthdays and drafts the messages, did a full 12-month expense breakdown across all my linked accounts, and helped me plan my son's 4th birthday with a huge vetted venue list.

It's also handled the unglamorous stuff: splitting Norway trip expenses with friends, building a dispute case for a parking ticket, monitoring YouTube channels for new videos and summarizing them, and doing due-diligence research on a real estate investment.

What I like most is it follows through. It sets up the recurring checks, remembers context, and shows its work with sources instead of guessing. Easily the most useful AI app I've tried.

Love how daily capabilities are being added.

title: It’s on an another level
content:
I started using Muse as just another chatbot, but I quickly realized it’s much more than that. It actually feels like I’m working with a highly intelligent, personal assistant, someone who understands me and helps me make better decisions.

My use cases are still pretty limited because I’m new to this. I’m still figuring out how much information and access I’m comfortable providing to really take advantage of its capabilities. But I’m slowly getting there.

What I’ve found so far is that Muse is incredibly useful and intelligently designed. Give it a try. Take it slow. Ask it the things you’d ask a good buddy, and maybe even the things you’d hesitate to ask someone because you don’t want to be judged or hurt their feelings.

Muse doesn’t mind. In fact, it almost encourages you to push back.

Just give it a shot.

title: Surprisingly Really Good
content:
I don’t trust Meta, and you shouldn’t either. I can only guess at what they plan to do with your “deep personal context” that they are collecting with this app. But they’ve made a lot of commitments to privacy with Muse, including the promise of end to end encryption, that hides your messages from meta entirely. But regardless, if you’re willing to forfeit some of that privacy, this app is shockingly useful for a chatbot.

For standard administrative work (like your day, planning a vacation, scheduling meetings, etc) this thing is amazing, and it’s really easy to connect to outside apps like calendar or Gmail, to work around other events you’ve already planned. I find it more pleasant than Gemini or ChatGPT which is my default for this type of work.

For pricing, the free tier goes you more than enough usage a majority of use cases. I haven’t tried doing complex work, like heavy coding or math, but I really don’t think that’s where you’ll get the most use out of this app.

I think the best use case for this app is influencers or business owners who manage social media accounts on Meta platforms, so if that’s you, definitely try this app.

I don’t fall into that category, but I still think this is the most useful chatbot I’ve ever tried.

title: My go-to personal agent
content:
Muse has become my go-to personal agent.

I've been testing it for a while and it's genuinely one of the most useful AI products I've used. It understands my context, helps me stay on top of my goals, proactively comes up with ideas for things it can build for me, and creates genuinely impressive artifacts.

What really stands out is the harness around the model. Muse doesn't feel like just another chatbot, it feels designed from the ground up to be a personal agent. Proactive without being annoying, a pleasure to talk to, and incredibly easy to set up and use.

I previously used OpenClaw, and the difference in setup and day-to-day usability is night and day. With Muse, you can just start using it and immediately get value.

A very impressive product, and already the personal agent I find myself reaching for first.

title: Already saved me time and money on the first day!
content:
I’m a husband and father taking care of a disabled wife and two kids while working full time. I need all the help I can get! I set up my muse with access to email, calendar, Facebook, messenger, Google Sheets and some other things. NGL: I am low-key terrified of what Facebook is going to do with all this data I’ve linked to it, but just on the first day, my muse drafted and sent emails to an insurance company, set up reminders about tasks, found me phone numbers to doctors offices, and did some research for me. It’s honestly amazing! Like any AI, these things are not going to be perfect, but having a personal assistant living in my phone that gets 90% of her jobs right is WAY better than not having a personal assistant (and probably on par with a human).

The only trivial complaint so far is the lack of text to speech so I can’t interact with it in the car. But given what else it seems capable of doing, that seems minor. Good job, Facebook!

title: Voiceover screen, reader Accessibility and navigation needs to improve.
content: Don’t get me wrong. I love the app! I believe it gives you more at no cost than any other agent. The limits reset weekly and you can ask it at any point how much of your quota you have used. It will tenaciously track airfare for you, make document Accessible, set price, Alerts and plan trips. It’s persistent memory and ability to connect to things that you use the most, make it in valuable. However you don’t always know when the agent has responded if you’re blind. And you can’t navigate through the list of messages by heading so when the main chat gets really long it becomes very difficult to get back to a particular topic. And there are unlabeled buttons. Overall, it’s the on boarding processes Accessible and I can definitely use the app for the basics. But I would certainly be giving it closer to five stars if they will resolve the Accessibility issues.
